prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the curved sidewalk, the raised retaining wall on the left (2 to 8 m away), and the vertical silhouettes of posts, trees, and the approaching silver SUV on the right. Across the five frames, the bright foreground shows the camera wearer advancing as a nearby left lamppost (about 1.5 to 2 m away in frame 1) disappears behind them, the silver SUV approaches from roughly 6 to 8 m in frame 1 to 3 to 4 m in frame 2 before exiting on the right edge at 2 to 3 m in frame 3, and a short curbside post (parking meter) moves closer from roughly 9 m in frame 1 to 2 to 3 m ahead on the right in frame 5, with nothing ever entering within arm's reach (under 1 m) of the wearer. Further back, a dark lawn sign on the left (decreasing from roughly 8 m to 3 m) and a lamppost with street signs ahead (decreasing from roughly 14 m to 6 m) stand several metres apart on opposite sides of the walkway. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the ground, the step change in elevation at the left retaining wall, and the exact depth ordering of overlapping tree canopies and posts immediately clear. However, the map is unreliable for the distant pedestrian 15 to 30 m down the sidewalk, who blends completely into the dark background alongside far buildings and sky, and it flattens the 3D geometry of the SUV and tree foliage into uniform grey silhouettes that hide which way anyone is facing.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates three discrete object classes against a black background: the silver `car` on the right roadway in frames 1 to 3, a `parking meter` post on the sidewalk in frames 1, 4, and 5, and a distant `person` on the walkway across all five frames. As the camera wearer walks forward, the `car` mask grows and shifts rightward from roughly 6 to 8 m ahead-right in frame 1 to 3 to 4 m in frame 2, becomes heavily truncated at the right image boundary at 2 to 3 m in frame 3, and leaves the view entirely in frames 4 and 5, while nothing comes within arm's reach of the wearer or the distant pedestrian. Meanwhile, a tiny `person` mask tracks the pedestrian roughly 15 to 30 m ahead along the sidewalk (positioned well behind and to the left of the car and curbside posts), and `parking meter` masks mark the near left post at 1.5 to 2 m in frame 1 and the right curbside post as it approaches from roughly 4 m to 2 m in frames 4 and 5. This map highlights the tiny distant pedestrian in frames 2 to 5 that is hard to spot in RGB alone and clearly shows when the car is partially out of view at the frame edge. However, it is unreliable in several places: it mislabels the upper canopy of a lamppost as a `person` in frame 1, misses the right curbside `parking meter` entirely in frames 1 to 3 while misclassifying the left lamppost in frame 1, omits all static scene layout (sidewalk, walls, signs, and buildings), and provides no 3D orientation or gaze information.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely black across all five frames, detecting neither the camera wearer nor any other person in the scene. Using the RGB strip for context, the camera wearer's own body and hands remain outside the field of view below the camera throughout the sequence, and nothing is held or reached for within arm's reach. The only visible pedestrian is roughly 15 to 30 m ahead down the sidewalk—spaced far behind the passing SUV (2 to 8 m away on the right in frames 1 to 3) and the curbside posts (2 to 12 m away)—and appears to walk away from or along the path while occupying only a few pixels, while any driver inside the approaching SUV is occluded by the windshield glare and vehicle body. Because no skeletons are rendered, the pose map adds no spatial information beyond confirming the absence of close-range visible bodies or hands that would be hard to see in RGB. Consequently, the map is completely unreliable for locating the distant pedestrian, estimating their facing direction or gaze toward the camera wearer, or tracking their movement across the five frames.
